info.text:
The 401(k) limit is up $6,500 since 2016: $18,000 in 2016 to $24,500 in 2026.
Every fall the IRS adjusts retirement limits and tax brackets for inflation. The 401(k) limit rounds down to $500 steps, so some years it doesn't move.
2026: 401(k) $24,500 (+$8,000 at 50+, +$11,250 at ages 60-63); IRA $7,500 (+$1,100 at 50+). Maxing a 401(k) over 26 paychecks is about $942 each.
The IRS usually posts the next year's numbers in October or November: check IRS.gov for 2027.
Source: IRS.
News and education, not financial advice.
